findings.title: Debris never shows when a hit opens a breach: the hitstop sets pdt to 0 on that frame and the opening is used up anyway
findings.claim: In interiorFeel.draw the breach opening is recorded every frame (`breachSeen = opened.seen`), but the burst only spawns `if (pdt > 0)`. A sector impact activates the breach and stamps `rooms.impactTick` in the same sim tick. So the frame that first sees the opening is also the frame `onHit` starts the 60 ms hitstop. `clock.advance(1/60)` then returns 0, the burst is skipped and the opening is never reported again. With the default `full` feel (and `reduced`), impact breaches never get their opening debris, which the spec requires (section 6: 'debris on the tick a breach opens').
findings.evidence: plan L1761-1762 (onHit runs before `clock.advance`), L1772-1773 (`breachSeen = opened.seen; if (pdt > 0) ... debrisBurst`); src/renderer/src/sim/debris.ts:L103-L109 (resolveImpact calls tryBreach -> activateBreach) and L117 (impactTick stamped in the same call); plan L1736 (`clock.hitstop(HITSTOP_SECONDS * f.hitstop)`, which is 0.06 for full and reduced); spec L89
findings.why: In ordinary play most breaches come from impacts, so a listed spec feature effectively never appears, and no test covers a hit and a breach opening on the same frame.
findings.fix: Spawn the burst whatever `pdt` is: `emitter.step(0)` neither ages nor moves particles, so the debris holds at the hole during the hitstop and then flies. Alternatively, update `breachSeen` only on frames where `pdt > 0`. Add an interiorFeel test: one frame with `hit: { rooms: [siteRoom] }` and `breaches.active[s]` going from 0 to 1, then a few frames later at least DEBRIS_COUNT visible sprites in `above.children[0]`.

findings.title: gradeCover returns overlapping rectangles, so the multiply darkens twice or three times along every wall
findings.claim: For a wall tile, gradeCover adds every floor part and every band arm from wallPicture. These overlap: n=floor adds {0,0,32,16}, nw/ne add the 16x16 quarters inside it, and the band hub and arms span y 10..22, crossing the floor half. Pixi 8 triangulates each rect in one path separately and fills them all, with no union. Under 'multiply' each overlapping triangle blends again, giving dst x (1 - a + a c)^n. Wall tiles next to rooms therefore show 2x-3x darker strips than the next floor tile, and the alert pulse (strength 0.35, #a53030) compounds there too. The duel flash, built from the same cover, double-brightens the same areas.
findings.evidence: plan L586-595 (gradeCover pushes `...p.floor, ...p.band` without merging), L1723 (`for (const r of cover) coverCtx.rect(...); coverCtx.fill(...)`), L1741 (flash from cover); src/renderer/src/render/wallModel.ts:L21-L35 (nw/ne quarters plus the n half; the band at LO=10..HI=22); src/renderer/src/render/doorModel.ts:L11 (PANEL_THICK 12, BAND 10); palette.json L24-L25 (ambient #a8b5b2, alert #a53030). The gradeModel test at plan L499-505 checks only the grid and the count of whole tiles, not overlap.
findings.why: A visible seam pattern along every wall in both views, worst at the alert peak, on the layer that is meant to unify the look. The owner gate is 'starts to look good'.
findings.fix: Make gradeCover return a cover with no overlaps: draw the union of floor and band for each wall tile (or for the whole ship) onto an art-pixel mask and emit merged row runs. Add a test that draws every cover rect onto art-pixel cells and asserts no cell is covered twice, and that the union equals floor/door tiles plus the wall floor and band union.

findings.title: In the sector, stars are 2 internal px but the ship's art pixel is 2 x fit.scale, so the picture mixes pixel sizes
findings.claim: Deviation (e) draws every star as 2 internal pixels. The sector world's art pixel is 2 x fit.scale internal pixels, and worldFit snaps that to whole screen pixels: for example, at stage 1.5 with fit 0.667, an art pixel is 2 screen px but a star is 3. The spec asks for 'stars of one art pixel'. The renderer already has that size every frame (`artPx = 2 * fit.scale`, plan L2281), so the stated reason ('depends on the world scale') does not need a fixed 2 px.
findings.evidence: plan L57, L1458 and L1808 (`starG.rect(s.x, s.y, 2, 2)`), spec note L2714, spec L105; src/renderer/src/render/worldFit.ts:L10 (art pixel = 2 x worldScale x stageScale, snapped)
findings.why: Pixels of two sizes in one frame is the mixed-pixel look the Art-i bible works against. In the duel (fit 1) the stars happen to match, so this affects only the sector.
findings.fix: Pass `frame.artPx` to `stars()` and to the star draw: size = artPx, positions snapped to multiples of artPx inside the band, speeds of 4 and 10 x artPx per second. The lightsModel test then takes artPx as a parameter.

findings.title: Deviation (f): console desks and screens are still off the art-pixel grid, and the blink cursor test allows a 1-unit overflow
findings.claim: DESK_W is 19, SCREEN_D is 3, the screen insets are odd and the desk outline is a 1-unit stroke, so desks and screens sit on half art pixels. Art-i-a's grid work missed them. The plan states this but leaves it. Its new cursor sits on that off-grid strip, and the screenCursor test accepts the cursor running 1 unit (half an art pixel) past the screen (`<= ... + s.w + 1`). This plan's own constraint says every procedural rectangle is whole art pixels.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/src/render/consoleModel.ts:L15 (DESK_W = round(19.2) = 19, SCREEN_D = 3), L45-L47 (odd offsets); src/renderer/src/render/consoleLayer.ts:L18 (stroke width 1); plan L17 (constraint), L1355 (the +1 tolerance), L2715 (note 6)
findings.why: Consoles are central to the interior and the only procedural interior art still off the grid. The new blink highlights the misalignment. Fixing it now costs a few constants and a test, against a separate pass later.
findings.fix: Either add a small task (DESK_W 20, DESK_D 10, SCREEN_D 2 or 4, even insets, outline width 2 with alignment 1, an onGrid test over every `deskPicture` side and flush combination, then tighten the screenCursor bound to the screen), or record it explicitly for the owner as an open Art-i-a defect in the Task 9 report.

findings.title: InteriorFeel has no destroy(), so every duel restart leaks four shared GraphicsContexts
findings.claim: interiorFeel creates `coverCtx` and three glow contexts and hands them to Graphics via `new Graphics(ctx)`. A Graphics destroys only a context it owns, so `container.destroy({ children: true })` in interiorView.destroy leaves these four contexts and their GPU-side context data. duelMode rebuilds the interior on every restart (and on dispose), so they pile up for the session.
findings.evidence: plan L1701 and L1710 (shared contexts), L1728-1729 and L1798 (`new Graphics(ctx.*)`), L1815-1819 (reset only, no destroy); plan L2456 (interiorView.destroy); src/renderer/src/app/duel/duelMode.ts:L80 and L111 (rebuilt on restart, destroyed on dispose)
findings.why: This is the lifetime question in review item 11. The leak is small but unbounded across restarts in one session.
findings.fix: Add `destroy()` to InteriorFeel that destroys `coverCtx` and `ctx.console`, `ctx.fire` and `ctx.lamp` (after the Graphics that use them), and call `fx.destroy()` from interiorView.destroy before `container.destroy`.

findings.title: The presentation clock keeps running while the game is paused, unlike the duel's existing fx
findings.claim: duelMode steps the tactical fx with `runtime.paused() ? 0 : dt`, but the interior (and the sector renderer) passes real `dt` to the feel. While paused, embers, smoke, vent puffs, the starfield and the alert pulse keep moving, the hit smoke times out and the interior shake decays, while the Helm and Weapons fx freeze.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/src/app/duel/duelMode.ts:L84 (stepFx frozen while paused), L87 (interior.draw with dt); plan L2451 (fx.draw with dt), L2281 (sector feel.draw with dt)
findings.why: The pause behaves differently in the two views of one mode. This is minor and the spec says nothing, but it is cheap to make consistent.
findings.fix: Pass a paused flag or a presentation dt into `fx.draw` (`runtime.paused() ? 0 : dt` in the duel; the session's paused phase in the sector) while keeping the real dt for `tiles.update`. Or state the choice as a decision.
